scenes.text: Your app sends every question to a big AI model. Most are easy. You pay big-model prices anyway.
What if a small model took the easy ones, and learned the hard ones? That's Apprentice: an open-source gateway that speaks the OpenAI API.
Change one base URL, and your app never knows.
First stop, the student: Kwen three, one point seven billion parameters, running on your machine through Ollama. Its answers cost nothing per token.
Small models slip up, so a judge checks every answer. Meet Kev, a tiny open model.
Fine-tuning on Colab took Kev from forty-six to ninety-nine percent accuracy.
Kev scores its confidence. Zero point eight or higher, the answer goes straight back.
Lower, and it escalates to the teacher: G L M five point two, a big open-weight model.
The trick: every teacher answer goes into memory.
When a similar question arrives, the student gets that worked example and usually solves it alone.
So the student takes more traffic over time, and the bill shrinks.
We tested it on eighty held-out text-to-S Q L questions.
New student: twenty-five percent. Teacher: one hundred. Apprentice, after learning: ninety-seven and a half.
The student handled eighty-six percent of requests, and the bill was eighty-seven percent smaller than teacher-only.
The catch: on question shapes it has never seen, Apprentice gets fifty-three percent, the student alone thirty-three. Memory works best on repeats.
Real questions repeat. A shop owner asks, in Hinglish, which store had the most orders. The student answers alone, for free.
A support bot answering refund questions. When the student answers, your data never leaves your machine.
Apprentice. Open source, open models, M I T licensed.
